newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on South American weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on South American weather.

text.p: Corn futures on the CBOT settled higher Monday on ideas that the corn crop in Argentina was in jeopardy, but gains were trimmed by a late sell-off in the soybean pit, CBOT traders said.
Talk has swept the market that southern Argentina needed more rain, but many traders with clients in that country said the crop was doing fine and were leery of the market's climb.
"If this is a weather market, then we could see them take out all these gains tomorrow (Tuesday)," said Joel Karlin, analyst with Everen Securities in Chicago.
On the day, Refco sold 2.5 million bushels March, Tenco bought 6 million March, and Cargill bought 1.5 million March. Continental Grain sold 1 million bushels March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 38,000 contracts, above the 36,334 traded Friday.
In options trading, Continental Grain sold 1,000 March $2.60 calls and Term Commodities bought 800 March $2.50 puts, pit sources said.
